la:verb:conor.html:
cōnor, ātus, 1,
v. dep., to undertake, endeavor, attempt, try, venture, presume, etc. (freq. and class.; syn. molior,; opp. facere,; opp. perficere,); constr. with acc., inf., rarely with abl. of the gerund., or absol.
With acc. (mostly of indef. objects): quicquam fallaciae,: istuc,: idem,: opus magnum et arduum,: id quod conantur,: multa,; : tantum scelus, id. Fragm. ap. ; cf.: tantam rem,: muita stulte,; : plurima frustra,.—
With inf. (freq.): hoc dicere,: aliquid facere,: me labefactare,: poëtas attingere,: versus pangere,: pueris absinthia dare,; : facere id quod constituerant,: invito transire,: tela mittere,; ; .—*
With abl. gerundii: ne frustra dehortando impedire conemini,that you attempt not vainly to dissuade,.—
With si: saepius noctu, si perrumpere possent, conati,. —(ε) Absol.: dum moliuntur (mulieres), dum conantur, annus est,: conari manibus pedibus noctisque et dies,: conantibus, priusquam id effici posset, adesse Romanos nuntiatur,: qui prius cogitare quam conari consuesset,before he proceeded to the undertaking,: ego obviam conabar tibi,: audax ad conandum,.—
Hence, subst.: cōnāta, ōrum, n., in pass. signif., an undertaking, attempt, venture, hazard (class.), Att. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; sq.; ; et saep.
